I'm 64 this year, been farming these same fields for 40 years. Went to middle school, so I can read the extension pamphlets they post at the village office, but to be honest I trust what I've seen with my own eyes and what my neighbors do more than what some young technician tells me. I've got 19.1 mu total — 12 mu I do wheat then maize, that's my main system, and 7.1 mu in cotton. My wife and I do most of the farm work. My two sons work construction in Shijiazhuang, send some money back, but they're not here for planting or harvest. My daughter-in-law helps when the factory gives her time off.

The wheat went in last October 8th. I used my own saved seed — local variety, not the fanciest hybrid but I know how it behaves. I put down base fertilizer then, about 15 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's April and the wheat is greening up decent. I'm going to topdress with urea around Qingming, about 10 kg per mu. If it looks yellow at heading I might throw on another 5 kg, but I'll judge when I see it. Three irrigations total: now for green-up, one at jointing, and one at grain filling. Pumping costs about 25 yuan each time, and they meter the well water now, not like the old days. I'll spray herbicide once, and fungicide only if I see disease starting.

For cotton, I'll plant around April 22nd. Same improved variety as last year — I'm not buying those expensive hybrids when this one does fine and the seed is cheaper. I'll put compound fertilizer in the rows before planting, about 20 kg per mu. Cotton is picky about water — too much and it grows too tall and lazy, too little and the bolls drop. I'll irrigate twice, three times only if July is bone dry. The bollworm is the real enemy. I'll spray insecticide 3-4 times and herbicide twice. Picking is the hard part — my wife and I will do the main picking, but I'll hire some women from the village for 40 yuan a day plus lunch during the peak pick in September.

Maize has to go in right after wheat comes off — June 8th or 10th. That window is tight, sometimes only five or six days if weather turns. I hire Zhang's tractor for plowing and planting, costs me 30 yuan per mu. I buy hybrid maize seed every year, about 2.5 kg per mu at 45 yuan — you can't save hybrid seed, it doesn't breed true. I put compound fertilizer down at planting, about 15 kg per mu, then topdress with urea at the 6-leaf stage, another 10 kg per mu. Water it twice, three times in a dry year.

Fertilizer prices are up again this year, so I'm watching every yuan. But I'm not cutting my rates much — last year I got 450 kg/mu of wheat and 480 kg/mu of maize, decent years. At my age, I'd rather spend a bit more and waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad yield that could really hurt us. A loss year hurts more than a good year helps. Total costs will run about 10,000 yuan. The wheat and maize give me stable grain income I can sell to the grain station, and cotton prices have been holding. That's my plan — steady as she goes, no big gambles when you're 64.
